definitions.explanation: The feeling of sadness or displeasure caused by unfulfilled hopes or expectations.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}に{落|お}ちて{失望|しつぼう}した。
examples.english: I was disappointed when I failed the exam.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}には{失望|しつぼう}させられた。
examples.english: I was disappointed by his attitude.

examples.japanese: {期待|きたい}が{大|おお}きかっただけに、{失望|しつぼう}も{大|おお}きかった。{何|なに}も{言|い}えずに{黙|だま}ってその{場|ば}を{離|はな}れた。
examples.english: Because my expectations were high, my disappointment was equally great. Unable to say anything, I quietly left the place.

notes:
{失望|しつぼう} expresses disappointment or loss of hope, typically when expectations are not met.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {失望|しつぼう}する (to be disappointed)
- {失望|しつぼう}させる (to disappoint someone)
- {失望|しつぼう}を{感|かん}じる (to feel disappointment)
- 〜に{失望|しつぼう}する (to be disappointed in/by ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {失望|しつぼう}: disappointment (formal, stronger emotion)
- がっかり: disappointment (casual, everyday expression)
- {落胆|らくたん}: discouragement, dejection (written/formal)

REGISTER: Somewhat formal. In casual conversation, がっかりする is more common.
